blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Between June 2026 and September 2026, detached houses: listings fell from 53 in June to 34 in September (−35.8%), and it took 26.5% of the city’s 136 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings fell from 108 in June to 96 in September (−11.1%), and it took 58.2% of the city’s 165 sales over the period.

The monthly write-ups singled out Clayton for detached houses in July, August, September (a sellers’ best bet); detached houses in June (a buyers’ best bet); condos and townhomes in June, July, August, September (a sellers’ best bet).

Fee-simple lots are the default form

Bare-land strata — the form, no Clayton instance verified: A bare-land strata lot is strata tenure ON the lot itself: the buyer takes a strata lot, pays strata fees, is bound by the strata's bylaws, and is entitled to a Form B Information Certificate for the lot — it is not fee-simple ownership with a road association. Tenure is read lot by lot on title.

Lot character — as the research states it, no invented sizes: The research states no Clayton-wide lot-size table. Any specific lot's zone, area and subdivision minimum are a parcel check against Surrey Zoning Bylaw No. 12000 — UNCONFIRMED per lot here.
ALR vs non-ALR split: Clayton Heights runs to the ALR in the north and west; the community-wide ALR share for Clayton is UNVERIFIED — no official source opened states it.

Assemblies / proposals — documented AS SUCH, never as inventory: The West Clayton mixed-use urban centre adjacent to a future rapid transit station at 184 Street and Fraser Highway, and the two named SkyTrain stations, are plan facts — not lots for sale and not current service. A lot near Fraser Highway carries plan upside and plan uncertainty until the designations and station are in place.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Clayton

items.t: Clayton is a board sub-area of the Fraser Valley board community "Cloverdale" (Clayton, Cloverdale, Serpentine) and a neighbourhood inside the City of Surrey's Cloverdale community, one of the City's seven communities.

Municipal geography: the City plans this ground as Clayton Heights — approximately 809 hectares (2,000 acres), extending from Fraser Highway in the south to the Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) in the north and west, bordered by the Township of Langley in the east. The City's plan neighbourhoods are East Clayton, West Clayton and the not-yet-initiated North Clayton.
East Clayton is located north of Fraser Highway along the border with the Township of Langley; homes east of that boundary are in the Township, not Surrey Clayton.

Planning frame: the Clayton General Land Use Plan (approved January 25, 1999) set up the Neighbourhood Concept Plan process; East Clayton's NCP was endorsed in 2003 and West Clayton's final NCP was approved in July 2015, planned for over 12,000 residents with a mixed-use centre at 184 Street and Fraser Highway. The City records that those NCP designations have been superseded by the Surrey 2050 OCP update — confirm a lot's current OCP designation rather than relying on an NCP label alone.
Civic anchor: Clayton Community Centre, 7155 187A Street, opened October 16, 2021 — a 75,000 sq. ft. facility integrating arts, recreation, library, parks and community amenities.
Catchments are address-based and no SD36 locator run for a Clayton address is on record: UNVERIFIED per address. ( read 2026-11-01)

Transit plan fact: the Surrey Langley SkyTrain project names Hillcrest-184 Street Station (northwest corner of 184 Street and Fraser Highway) and Clayton Station (future intersection of 190 Street and Fraser Highway); TransLink states a 16-km Expo Line extension with an anticipated in-service date of 2029 — a plan, not current service.

Market context, labelled community context ONLY (SnapStats FVR September 2026; land has NO SnapStats category): Clayton detached 34 / 10 / 29%; Clayton "Condos & Townhomes" combined 96 / 20 / 21% — the highest ratios in the Cloverdale sub-area set that month. Cloverdale community medians (sub-area medians are not published): detached $1,212,500; attached $740,000. No detached figure is a land figure.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Clayton

items.t: BC strata block (wherever a bare-land strata lot is the purchase — form only; no Clayton instance verified): Form B within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25¢/page; depreciation reports every 5 years for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss. 123.1/123.2, May 1, 2023 exemptions). A "45+" listing line is NOT a valid age bylaw.

ALR block (Clayton's north and west edge parcels): ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; Strata Property Act s. 239; Agricultural Land Commission Act s. 21(1)); subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; principal residence ≤500 m², a suite within the principal residence only, and one additional residence of 90 m² (parcels ≤40 ha) or 186 m² (parcels >40 ha).

BC Assessment farm class — full three-tier form: $2,500 (farm operation 0.8–4 ha); $2,500 plus 5% of the actual value of the area over 4 ha (>4 ha); $10,000 (under 0.8 ha); applications by October 31. A flat "$2,500+" statement is an error and is not used here.

First-home programs: The FTHB GST rebate (Bill C-4, Royal Assent March 13, 2026; 100% to $1M, maximum $50,000, phasing to $1.5M, window March 20, 2025–2031) applies to new HOUSING, not bare land. New Housing Rebate: 36% / maximum $6,300 / $350,000–$450,000. HBP $60,000; FHSA $40,000 / $8,000 per year.

Clayton moved faster than the rest of Cloverdale in September 2026. Clayton's detached sales ratio was 29% and attached 21%, ahead of the Cloverdale sub-area (13% / 17%), while Serpentine was 0 / 0 / NA in both splits.

The NCP labels are superseded. East and West Clayton NCP designations have been superseded by the Surrey 2050 OCP update — a lot marketed on an old NCP label still needs its current OCP designation confirmed with the City.
Census for Clayton: UNVERIFIED.

faq.q: Are there more or fewer homes for sale in Clayton than in June?
faq.a: In Clayton, listings of houses fell from 53 in June to 34 in September (−35.8%); condos and townhomes fell from 108 in June to 96 in September (−11.1%).

faq.q: How big is Clayton compared with the rest of Cloverdale?
faq.a: In September 2026, Clayton held 16.9% of the 201 houses listed in Cloverdale and 49.5% of the 194 condos and townhomes listed in Cloverdale.

faq.q: How many homes sold in Clayton from June to September 2026?
faq.a: 36 houses and 96 condos and townhomes sold in Clayton over those 4 months.

faq.q: Who can help me buy or sell in Clayton?
faq.a: Jared Gibbons, REALTOR® with Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, works across the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver. Call or text 604-928-1361 or use the contact form on this site.

faq.q: How do I find out which school serves an address in Clayton?
faq.a: School catchments are set by address, so use the school district's catchment locator with the exact address. Catchment lines change, so check before you write an offer.

faq.q: Is there a vacant lot I can buy in Clayton?
faq.a: No bare-land subdivision is verified in the research — the purchase is an existing fee-simple house lot for rebuild / added units, or an ALR-edge parcel.

faq.q: Is Clayton in Surrey or Langley?
faq.a: Surrey. Clayton Heights runs from Fraser Highway to the ALR, bordered by the Township of Langley in the east — homes east of that boundary are in the Township, with different bylaws, taxes and school district.

faq.q: How many units can a Clayton lot hold?
faq.a: 3 under 280 m², 4 over 280 m², up to 6 on eligible 281 m²+ lots within 400 m of a frequent bus stop — subject to zone, servicing and, on ALR parcels, the ALC caps instead.

faq.q: Can I add a coach house?
faq.a: In zones that allow detached houses, duplexes and houseplexes, yes — 35–75 m² (up to 120 m² on RA, R2, R2-O and R3 lots below maximum FAR), lane access required for a coach house on smaller R3–R6 lots, one extra parking space.

faq.q: The listing says "RF-12" — is that the lot's zone?
faq.a: Not currently: RF-12 / RF-12C became R4 and RF-SD became R6 on July 8, 2024. Check the lot's current zone in Bylaw 12000 before quoting potential.
